title: Midpoint dating shifted one-harmonic insect peaks by less than 0.02 day in four samples in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020
abstract: We compared midpoint dating with exact collection-window integration for seasonal insect catch peaks. Four latitude samples used 4,409 catches at 136 traps in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020. Absolute one-harmonic peak shifts were below 0.02 day. Two-harmonic fits gave shifts of at most 0.2 day. Catch peaks preceded fitted temperature peaks by 13.7 to 19.8 days, but model shape changed some lags by several days. A constant-window identity explains phase stability despite amplitude changes. Selected long-coverage traps, missing records, shared annual weather and one year per country limit inference. We establish no causal weather effect, climate trend or pollution effect. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. Raw data remain external.

display.caption: Seasonal catch and temperature curves in four geographic samples. Curves have zero mean and unit amplitude. Midpoint and interval catch curves nearly overlap.
